# The Last Timeline — Dana Whitfield
## Test script — FICTIONAL

**Recording date:** November 24, 2026. A made-up case (every name, place and date is invented) written to test the true-crime
detectors on wording the Javits script never uses: a sheriff's office, deputies, a magistrate, a bond, a plea, months not days.

## Chapter 1 — Dana

Nineteen-year-old Dana Whitfield was a nursing student at Calder Community College in Westbrook. She worked evenings at the Pine Street Diner and lived with her mother, Carol Whitfield. Her mother said Dana planned to become a pediatric nurse.

## Chapter 2 — The last night

On March 3, 2025, Dana Whitfield worked her last shift at the Pine Street Diner. At 10:12 that night, she closed out the register, deputies said. At 10:40, a parking-lot camera recorded her walking to her car. At 11:05, her phone connected to a cell tower near Lake Corrie.

## Chapter 3 — The search

On March 4, 2025, Whitfield was reported missing by her mother. On March 5, 2025, her car was found at a boat ramp on Lake Corrie. On March 9, 2025, searchers found her body in the woods north of the lake; she had been killed.

## Chapter 4 — The investigation

The Calder County Sheriff's Office led the investigation. Sheriff Ray Okafor called two coworkers persons of interest. Okafor said deputies do not believe her mother's boyfriend was involved. Okafor added that Thomas Reed remains under investigation. Okafor described the killing as “a deliberate act by someone she knew.”

## Chapter 5 — The evidence

Investigators obtained doorbell video from homes along Lakeview Road. Investigators said the footage showed a pickup truck headed to the boat ramp, then a man walked to Lakeview Road. Deputies recovered Whitfield's phone from the lake. Fingerprints on the driver's door were matched to Thomas Reed. The murder weapon was never recovered.

## Chapter 6 — Two accounts

Where Reed spent that night became the center of the case. Detective Lena Cruz said Reed was alone at the boat ramp that night. Defense attorney Paul Danner said Reed was with two friends at a bar in Westbrook. The two accounts could not both be true.

## Chapter 7 — The arrest

The summer passed without an answer for the family. On August 14, 2025, deputies arrested 41-year-old Thomas Reed at his home in Westbrook. It had been more than five months since Whitfield was killed. Her mother said she could finally sleep.

## Chapter 8 — In court

The case then moved to the courts. At a bond hearing on August 18, 2025, Reed appeared before Magistrate Helen Ortiz in Calder County Municipal Court. He was charged with second-degree murder and tampering with evidence. Ortiz ordered him held on $750,000 bond.

## Chapter 9 — The plea

On February 10, 2026, Reed pleaded guilty to voluntary manslaughter under a plea agreement. Circuit Judge Mark Haley accepted the plea and sentenced Reed to twenty years in prison. Carol Whitfield said no sentence would bring her daughter back.
